The claim for compensation raised in this claim petition is in respect of fatal injuries alleged to have been sustained by the deceased Sh. Rohit Kumar in a motor accident that took place on 17.02.2020, at about 11:45 pm, Near CNG Pump, Outer Ring Road Flyover, Ber Sarai, New Delhi,
regarding which one FIR No.0061/2020, under Sections 279/304A IPC was registered at PS Kishangarh.

The vehicle involved in this case is a car bearing registration No. UP-23T- 6427, which at the relevant time of accident was being driven by respondent no. 1 (R1), owned by respondent no.
2 (R2) and insured with respondent no. 3 (R3).

sentences.text:
Case of the petitioners is that on 17.02.2020, the deceased was going on foot towards R.K. Puram,
Sector-3 from Munrika.

When he reached near CNG Pump, Outer Ring Road Flyover, Ber Sarai,
New Delhi, the offending vehicle bearing registration No. UP-23T-6427, which was being driven by respondent no. 1 at a very high speed and in rash and negligent manner, came and hit the deceased with great force due to which he fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
It is further stated that the deceased was removed to JPNA Trauma Centre, AIIMS, New Delhi where his MLC was prepared and he died during the course of his treatment.
His postmortem was also conducted.
3. Respondents no. 1 and 2 have not filed their replies either to the DAR or to the claim petition.

4. Respondent no. 3 has filed its reply wherein it is stated that they have issued 'Package Policy Commercial Vehicle (Passenger Carrying)' in respect of the alleged offending vehicle in the name of respondent no. 2 which was valid for the period from 20.11.2019 to 19.11.2020 subject to terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
It is further stated that the respondent no. 1 had been issued driving license valid for LMV (NT) vehicles.
It was not a valid and effective driving license for purpose of driving commercial vehicle.
The offending vehicle being driven by R-1 was a taxi which is a commercial vehicle.

It is further stated that the Investigating Officer did not place on record the verification report of permit of the offending vehicle and hence, the Insurance Company is not liable to compensate the petitioners.
5.

On 04.10.2021, the following issues were framed by this tribunal as:-
1.

Whether the deceased sustained fatal injuries in the accident which occurred on 17.02.2020 at about 11:45 PM, Near CNG Pump, Outer Ring Road Flyover, Ber Sarai,
New Delhi caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. UP-23T-6427 being driven by respondent no. 1, owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 3 ? OPP.
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?

OPP. 
3. Relief.
6.
In support of their claim, the petitioner no. 1/mother of deceased examined herself as PW1.

Petitioners examined Sh.
Bharat, an eye witness of the accident as PW2.

In rebuttal, the respondent no. 3 examined Sh.
Raghunath Pawar, Assistant Manager as R3W1.
7.

The Tribunal heard the arguments advanced by Sh. Sh. A.K. Jha, Ld. Counsel for petitioners and Sh. R.K. Tripathi, Ld. Counsel for R-3/Insurance Company and has carefully perused the entire record of the case as well as written submissions filed on behalf of petitioners.
The findings on the aforementioned issues are rendered hereinafter in the succeeding paragraphs.

sentences.text: Whether the deceased sustained fatal injuries in the accident which occurred on 17.02.2020 at about 11:45 PM, Near CNG Pump, Outer Ring Road Flyover, Ber Sarai, New Delhi caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. UP-23T-6427 being driven by respondent no. 1, owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 3 ? OPP.
9. Onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioners.
The first question that needs to be decided is whether the accident was caused by the vehicle bearing registration No. UP- 23T-6427.

In order to prove the same, the petitioners have examined Sh. Bharat, an eye witness of the accident, as PW2 who tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW2/A. He deposed that on 17.02.2020, at about 11:45 pm, he was present at his Momos shop near CNG Pump, Outer Ring Road, Flyover, Ber Sarai,
New Delhi and saw the deceased going towards Sector-3, R.K. Puram from Munrika as pedestrian.

He further deposed that when the deceased reached near CNG Pump, Outer Ring Road Flyover, Ber Sarai (infront of his shop), one white colour Wagon R car/taxi bearing registration No. UP-23T6427,
being driven by its driver at a very high speed and in rash and negligent manner, came from Munrika side and hit the deceased with great force due to which the deceased fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
He further deposed that the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of driver of said car/taxi.
10. During cross examination, he deposed that the accident took place in his presence.
He further deposed that he used to sell momos on rehri from 4 pm to 11 pm.
He further deposed that he did not inform the police, but since the deceased was his neighbour, he rushed to his home to call the relative of deceased.
He further deposed that the deceased was crossing the road from Zebra Crossing at the time of accident.
He denied the suggestion that the accident occurred due to negligence of deceased.

11. In cases National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287 and United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Deepak Goel and Ors., 2014 (2) TAC 846 (Del.) decided by the Coordinate Bench of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court, it was held that "......where the petitioners filed either the certified copies of the criminal record or the criminal record showing the completion of investigation by police or issuance of charge sheet under Section 279/304A IPC or the certified copy of FIR or the recovery of the mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle, then these documents are sufficient proof to reach to a conclusion that the driver was negligent particularly when there is no defence available from the side of driver."
12.

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court in Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303 has observed that filing of charge sheet against the driver prima facie points towards his complicity in driving the vehicle rashly and negligently.

entities.text: Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has been further observed that even when the accused were to be acquitted in the criminal case, the same may be of no effect on the assessment of the liability required in respect of motor accident cases by the Tribunal.

13. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a Civil Court and in Civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as are required in a criminal prosecution.

Reference in this regard is made to the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported as Santosh vs Mohd. Uvais And Ors on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175166551/
3 (2009) 13 SC 530 in Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others,
wherein it has been observed that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the petitioners and the petitioners were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
14.

Therefore, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against the respondent no. 1 in terms of judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi passed in the case of Cholamandalam M.S.
General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.

sentences.text:
In view of foregoing discussion, it stands proved on preponderance of probability that the aforesaid accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing registration no. UP-23T-6427 and the said vehicle at that time was driven by respondent no. 1,
owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 3.
Hence, this issue is decided in favour of the petitioners and against the respondents.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?

17. As rashness and negligence on part of driver of the offending vehicle/respondent No. 1 has been proved, the petitioners have become entitled to be compensation for death of their family member in the said accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
The compensation to which the petitioners are entitled shall be under the heads as discussed hereinafter.
(i) Loss of dependency 18.

The petitioner No. 1 being mother of the deceased has stepped into the witness box as PW1 and filed her evidence by way of affidavit as Ex. PW1/A wherein, she has claimed that her deceased son was working as Patient Caretaker/Attendant with Nestiva Hospital, JS Complex 384, Near Canara Bank, Munrika, New Delhi-110067 and was getting salary of Rs.18,500/- per month.
During cross examination, she admitted that she had not placed on record any document with regard to the vocation and income of her deceased son.

She has tendered on record copy of educational qualification certificates of deceased as Ex. PW1/2 (colly), as per which the deceased had passed matriculation examination in the year 2014 and intermediate examination in the year 2016.

19. Since the employment and income of the deceased has not been established on record, the minimum wages of matriculates is taken into account as per rates prevalent in Delhi, which was Rs.
17,991/- per month at the time of accident.

20. In order to prove the age of deceased, PW1 has tendered on record copy of PAN card and Aadhaar card of deceased as Ex. PW1/3 and Ex. PW1/4 respectively, in which the date of birth of deceased is found recorded as 01.07.1996.
Hence, going by these documents, the age of deceased as on the date of accident i.e. on 17.02.2020 was 23 years, 7 months and 16 days.

In terms of law laid Santosh vs Mohd. Uvais And Ors on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175166551/
4 down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr., (2009) 6 SCC 121, which has also been approved by the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.,
(2017) 16 SCC 680, the multiplier of '18' is applicable in the present case.

sentences.text: 21. Now coming to calculation of loss of dependency, the present claim petition has been filed by two petitioners i.e. mother and father of the deceased.
PW1 during cross examination has admitted that the deceased was unmarried at the time of accident.

Hence, in terms of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma & Ors. (Supra) and Pranay Sethi & Ors. (Supra), half of earnings of deceased shall be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.

22. Further, in view of the law laid down in the case of Pranay Sethi & Ors. (Supra), the petitioners are also held entitled to addition of 40% of earning of the deceased towards future prospects as the deceased was below the age of 40 years at the relevant time of accident.

Thus, the loss of dependency in the petitioners case comes to Rs.27,20,239/- (rounded off) {(Rs.17,991/-X 12 X 18 X 1/2 X 140/100)}.
(ii) COMPENSATION UNDER NON-PECUNIARY HEADS 23.

In terms of propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi (Supra), the petitioners are also held entitled to amount of Rs.15,000/- each under the head of loss of estate and funeral expenses, i.e. a total of Rs.30,000/-
under both heads.

LIABILITY 38.
During the course of final arguments, Ld. Counsel for Insurance Company has argued that the offending vehicle was not having valid permit at the time of accident.

39. In order to prove the same, the Insurance Company has examined on record one Sh. Raghunath Pawar, Assistant Manager from their office at R3W1 who tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. R3W1 and relied upon certified copy of insurance policy as Ex. R3W1/2, notice under Order 12 Rule 8 CPC as Ex. R3W1/3 along with its original postal receipts as Ex. R3W1/4 and Ex. R3W1/5.

He deposed that the Insurance Company had issued package policy commercial vehicles (passenger carrying) with regard to Maruti Wagon R car/taxi bearing registration No. UP-23T-6427 for the period from 20.11.2019 to 19.11.2020 in favour of respondent no. 2 Ashraf Ali subject to terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
He further deposed that the respondent no. 1 was having driving license which was valid for driving LMV (NT) whereas he was driving taxi which is a commercial vehicle.
He further deposed that the owner of the offending vehicle did not have permit at the time of accident.

He further deposed that the Insurance Company had sent copy of notice under Order 12 Rule 8 CPC to the driver and owner of the offending vehicle to produce the original driving license,

sentences.text: During cross examination, he admitted that the offending vehicle was insured with their Company at the time of accident.
41. R-1 and R-2 did not enter into the witness box to refute the assertions of R3W1 or to prove valid driving license and permit in their favour.

42. In National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Chella Bharathamma & Ors (2004) 8 SCC 517, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held the view of High Court unjustified inasmuch as the High Court held that in case of no permit, the question of violation of any condition does not arise.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Chella Bharathamma & Ors (2004) 8 SCC 517
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court observed that a person without permit to ply a vehicle cannot be placed at a better pedestal vis-a-vis one who has a permit, but has violated any condition thereof.

It has been further observed that plying of a vehicle without a permit is an infraction, therefore, in terms of Section 149(2) of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, defence is available to the insurer on that aspect.
It was held that considering the beneficial object of the Act, the insurer was directed to satisfy the award, with liberty to recover the amount from the insured.
43. In view of foregoing discussion, respondent no. 3 being the insurer is liable to satisfy the award but is held entitled to recovery rights against the insured/respondent no.2.

Therefore, respondent no. 3 is first directed to deposit the award amount with UCO Bank, Patiala House Court Branch,
along with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition by RTGS/NEFT/IMPS in bank account being maintained in the above said bank in name of this tribunal within 30 days from today, failing which it is liable to pay interest at the rate of 9% per annum for the period of delay.

In case even after lapse of 90 days from today, respondent no. 3 fails to deposit this compensation with interest, in that event, in light of judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi passed in the case of New India Assurance Company Limited Vs. Kashmiri Lal 2007 ACJ 688, this compensation shall be recovered by attaching the bank account of respondent no. 3 with a cost of Rs.5,000/-.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
11. In cases National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287 and United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Deepak Goel and Ors., 2014 (2) TAC 846 (Del.) decided by the Coordinate Bench of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court, it was held that "......where the petitioners filed either the certified copies of the criminal record or the criminal record showing the completion of investigation by police or issuance of charge sheet under Section 279/304A IPC or the certified copy of FIR or the recovery of the mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle, then these documents are sufficient proof to reach to a conclusion that the driver was negligent particularly when there is no defence available from the side of driver."
12.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303 has observed that filing of charge sheet against the driver prima facie points towards his complicity in driving the vehicle rashly and negligently.
13. It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a Civil Court and in Civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as are required in a criminal prosecution.
Pertinently, respondent no. 1 himself was the best witness who could have stepped into the witness box to deny his involvement in the accident or to deny negligence on his part, which he failed to do.
Therefore, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against the respondent no. 1 in terms of judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi passed in the case of Cholamandalam M.S.
General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.
15.
17. As rashness and negligence on part of driver of the offending vehicle/respondent No. 1 has been proved, the petitioners have become entitled to be compensation for death of their family member in the said accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
